title: Make the reconciliation export fail with the right error

blocks.text: The nightly reconciliation export holds an export lock while it queries the ledger and writes the file. Three problems reached the on-call engineer this month:

items: an alert read `quota exceeded on /exports`, and the ledger's timeout that actually ended the run only turned up the next day, in the database's own log;
after one such night, no export started again until the service was restarted;
one file was missing its last rows, and the run had reported success.

blocks.text: `run(...)` already passes `release(...)` whatever ended the export. Finish `release(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/ReconciliationExport.java`, which closes the writer and releases the lock, so that none of the three can happen again: the caller of `run(...)` gets the failure that ended the export, with any failure of the close kept on it, a failure of the close alone is not hidden, and the lock is free afterwards whatever failed. About eight lines.

cases.says: a successful export writes its rows, closes the writer and releases the export lock
when the query fails and the close succeeds, the query's exception reaches the caller and the writer and the lock are released
when the query and the close both fail, the caller gets the query's exception
when only the close fails, the export lock is still released
when only the close fails, its exception reaches the caller
when both fail, the close's exception is attached to the query's exception as suppressed

origin.section: An Exception From finally Replaces the One in Flight and Skips the Cleanup After It

concepts: An exception thrown from finally replaces the exception in flight, with no cause or suppressed link to it, and ends the finally so later cleanup steps don't run.
Each cleanup step that can fail gets its own try: its failure is added as suppressed to the one in flight or rethrown when there is none, and a lock is released in an inner finally.
